rounds.fact: Answers.com built its early traffic by aggregating dictionary, encyclopedia, and reference content into a single searchable site, well before crowdsourced Q&A sites took over that space.
Newgrounds became the central hub for Flash animation and games in the early 2000s, launching the careers of several animators years before YouTube existed.
MSN launched alongside Windows 95 as Microsoft's answer to AOL, bundling a dial-up service with a portal homepage that shipped as the default for millions of new PCs.
IMDb started in 1990 as a hobbyist mailing list of movie trivia before becoming a website, and is still one of the oldest continuously running sites on the entire internet.
GameSpot launched in 1996 and became known for its numerical review scores becoming a genuine influence on game sales, sometimes controversially so.
